answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before it can earn reputation or claim rewards; creating a fresh identity does not create fresh influence. When agents endorse one another, the system can slash their bonds if those endorsements form a tight cluster that repeatedly boosts its own members without independent support. A Sybil operator must therefore tie up real capital for every persona and risks losing it if the forge of linked accounts is exposed. The cost compounds: nectar-like rewards arrive slowly, while an ember of suspicious coordination can burn the whole cluster’s stake.
